title: Splitting off the first coefficient block before pullback
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be any scheme morphism, $L$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $n,e\in\mathbb N$. Use the fixed tensor and degree comparison constructions of [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit]. Set $J=\ker(j)$, $P=\mathrm{tensorPullback}(j)$, $a=n(e+1)$, $b=n(0+1)$, $c=n((e+1)+1)$, and $F=P(J\otimes L^n)$. Define $k:(J\otimes L^b)\otimes L^a\to J\otimes L^c$ by the associator, $J\otimes\mathrm{tensorPowAddIso}(b,a)^{-1}$, and the arithmetic cast $b+a=c$. Then $P(k)\gg C_{e+1}=\delta_{J\otimes L^b,L^a}\gg((C_0\gg\rho_F)\otimes S_e)$, where $C_d$ is boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso at d, $S_e$ is boundarySectionDegreeIso at e, and $\delta$ is boundaryPullbackTensorIso. This is a morphism equality without invertibility or a symmetry of the L blocks.

source.place: Tag 09MS, coherent-equation-ses; canonical tensor comparisons from modules.tex, Tag 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), and Tag 01CA (section-tensor-product); read via the Stacks tag pages.

proof.text: Transport the Mathlib monoidal structure to P along boundaryPullbackComparison. Its tensorator is the inverse of boundaryPullbackTensorIso. The proved normalization of the monoidal unit identifies its unit with boundaryPullbackPowIso in degree zero.

Induct on a to show the recursive pullback power comparison respects tensorPowAddIso(a,b). The zero case is left unitality; the successor uses tensorator naturality and associativity. Then induct on d to show that pulling back n*d factors and grouping them into d blocks equals first grouping on X, then pulling back each block and comparing its n factors. Use the addition formula from the first induction, and naturality under arithmetic degree casts.

Induct on n to identify tensorPowAddIso(n,0).inv with the right unitor, and deduce the degree-one tensorPowMulIso formula. Expand the degree-zero coefficient comparison; right unitality identifies C_0 followed by its right unitor with P of the arithmetic cast n*1=n.

Expand the inverse positive-degree coefficient comparison at d. Expand tensorPowMulIso(n,d+1). Move its remaining-block map through the associator and pullback tensorator by naturality; the block-grouping identity from step 2 identifies the remaining factor with the inverse section-degree comparison. Cancel isomorphisms to obtain the forward splitting formula. Transport b=n*1 to n, using equality elimination for the product map and tensorator naturality for its pullback. This gives the exact displayed equation, including n=0 and e=0.

lean.statement:
theorem boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso_split {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    (L : X.Modules) (n e : ℕ) :
    let a := n * (e + 1)
    let b := n * (0 + 1)
    let c := n * ((e + 1) + 1)
    let k : (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow b) ⊗ L.tensorPow a ⟶
        j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow c :=
      (α_ _ _ _).hom ≫ j.ker.toModules ◁ (L.tensorPowAddIso b a).inv ≫
        j.ker.toModules ◁ (eqToHom (by
          dsimp [a, b, c]
          congr 1
          simp only [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one]
          omega) : L.tensorPow (b + a) ⟶ L.tensorPow c)
    (tensorPullback j).map k ≫ (boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso j L n (e + 1)).hom =
      (boundaryPullbackTensorIso j (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow b)
        (L.tensorPow a)).hom ≫
        (((boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso j L n 0).hom ≫
          (ρ_ ((tensorPullback j).obj (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow n))).hom) ⊗ₘ
          (boundarySectionDegreeIso j L n e).hom)
